comparison: Both evaluations support the CRISPR knockout generation and characterization (C39, C40, C88, C89). OpenEval explicitly evaluates off-target sequencing and protein truncation validation, while peer reviewers implicitly accept this methodological foundation without challenge. OpenEval also addresses the morpholino vs. knockout rationale (C114), which peer reviewers do not specifically mention.

Both evaluations support the cardiac phenotype characterization (C41, C42, C44, C76, C90, C91). OpenEval provides detailed statistical assessment and notes consistency with mouse phenotypes. Peer reviewers affirm the evidence is solid without specific challenges. Peer review includes additional claims C7 and C8 not mentioned in OpenEval's evaluation.

Perfect claim overlap (C45, C46, C77) regarding normal development and viability. Both evaluations support these findings. OpenEval emphasizes importance for interpreting CCM-specific effects, while peer reviewers accept these control findings without detailed commentary.

Perfect claim overlap (C9, C78, C97) regarding reduced CVP blood flow. Both evaluations support these hemodynamic findings. OpenEval notes marginal statistical significance (p=0.0346) but accepts the finding, while peer reviewers affirm the evidence is solid without expressing concerns about statistical power.

High claim overlap (C3, C4, C47, C48, C49, C50, C92, C93, C94, C95) on embryonic CCM reduction. Both evaluations strongly support this key genetic finding. OpenEval emphasizes robust sample sizes and statistical significance, while peer reviewers affirm solid evidence. OpenEval includes C34 which peer review groups with adult CCM data.

Strong claim overlap (C5, C35, C52, C53, C100, C101) on adult CCM reduction. Both evaluations support this major finding. OpenEval highlights consistency between embryonic and adult phenotypes and 3D quantification methodology. Peer review includes C69 (mechanism) which OpenEval addresses separately in R11.

High claim overlap (C6, C55, C56, C102, C103, C104, C105, C106) on pharmacological validation with propranolol and metoprolol. Both evaluations support these findings. OpenEval emphasizes β1-selectivity of metoprolol supporting specific mechanism, while peer reviewers accept therapeutic potential without detailed methodological commentary.

Perfect claim match (C57) on safety observations. OpenEval rates this as UNCERTAIN due to lack of quantitative data, while peer reviewers rate it as SUPPORTED, affirming the evidence is solid. This represents a clear disagreement on the rigor of this safety claim.

Perfect claim overlap (C10, C64, C79, C111, C112) on BDM cardiac inhibition experiments. Both evaluations support these findings as important mechanistic evidence for the hemodynamic hypothesis. OpenEval emphasizes robust sample sizes, while peer reviewers affirm solid evidence without specific concerns.

High claim overlap (C61, C63, C65, C66, C107, C108, C109, C110) on KLF2a independence. OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED with detailed statistical assessment, while peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN due to morpholino validation concerns and suboptimal masking methodology. This represents a significant disagreement on methodological rigor.

Moderate claim overlap (C11, C58, C67, C70) on central mechanistic conclusion about β1AR and hemodynamics. Both evaluations support this conclusion. OpenEval notes potential overstatement about sole mechanism given endothelial expression (C82), while peer reviewers emphasize translational relevance. Peer review includes C71 which OpenEval groups with therapeutic implications.

Minimal overlap (C82 only) on hemodynamic mechanism. OpenEval's R11 addresses broader mechanistic conclusions with caveats about endothelial contributions, while peer R10 focuses specifically on hemodynamic mechanism acceptance. Both support the general conclusion but OpenEval expresses more nuanced concerns.

Moderate claim overlap (C37, C72, C73, C74) on therapeutic potential and metoprolol advantages. Both evaluations support these translational implications. OpenEval emphasizes appropriate framing as hypothesis requiring validation, while peer reviewers highlight relevance to cardiovascular medicine. Peer review includes C36 and C38 which OpenEval addresses in R7.

Minimal overlap (C71 only) on therapeutic suggestions. OpenEval groups C71 with broader mechanistic conclusions (R11), while peer reviewers group it with therapeutic implications. Both support the claim but categorize it differently in their evaluations.

OpenEval evaluates claims C83, C84, C85 regarding β1AR expression patterns and tissue-specific contribution uncertainties. These methodological caveats are acknowledged as important limitations. No corresponding peer review evaluation specifically addresses these claims, though peer R11 mentions caveats about tissue-specific contributions remain to be addressed.
